note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 (independent auditor, after the round-trip unit's claim was rewritten to name runTransfer). Section 4: "In order to create a connection, each end of the connection chooses a TID for itself, to be used for the duration of that connection." and "The response to the request, under normal operation, uses a TID chosen by the server as its source TID". Producer at HEAD: serve -> handleRRQ validates the RRQ, takes a sem slot and starts go runTransfer; runTransfer dials the per-transfer socket (net.DialUDP at handler.go:343) and serves OACK and every DATA block on it, so the server's TID is chosen per transfer and held for its whole length. TestRFC1350ServerChoosesOneTIDForTheTransfer (real serve path via startTestTFTPServer) fails if any of three DATA blocks comes from the request port or from a port other than the first block's: both clauses, own TID and kept for the duration. TestListenTFTPLoopbackRoundTrip fails if the first DATA comes from port 69 and needs every block ACKed to that TID to complete the transfer; its rewritten claim (handleRRQ hands each RRQ to runTransfer, which dials a fresh socket) now matches the code and states no more than the body checks (it does not claim later blocks share the TID; the other unit proves that). Records: the round-trip unit's hand-written mutant (handler.go:321, DATA block 1 sent from mainConn instead of starting runTransfer) is exactly the claimed violation and its red is the unit's own source-port assertion, approved by ze-test-judge; the transfer unit's record is a revert of handleRRQ, which proves dependency only, so its TID assertions are judged by reading. {single-polarity: positive} holds: no input or config makes the server reply from port 69. The earlier prose finding (stale handler.go:293 citations in the claim and the rfc/short annotation) is resolved: both now name runTransfer. Evidence limit: on this host the integration unit SKIPs (bind lo:69 needs root); its green and red were observed in the QEMU guest by the recorder.
